claim: Eukaryotic ribosomal RNA (rRNA) is modified at more than 100 locations.
source: Eukaryotic ribosomal RNA (rRNA) is modified at more than 100 locations, particularly at highly conserved and functionally important nucleotides.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a general fact about eukaryotic rRNA.

claim: Eukaryotic rRNA modifications occur particularly at highly conserved and functionally important nucleotides.
source: Eukaryotic ribosomal RNA (rRNA) is modified at more than 100 locations, particularly at highly conserved and functionally important nucleotides.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a general characteristic of rRNA modifications.

claim: During ribosome biogenesis, modifications are added at various stages of assembly.
source: During ribosome biogenesis, modifications are added at various stages of assembly.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as background knowledge.

claim: No method exists to simultaneously evaluate the modification status at all sites within a single rRNA molecule.
source: The existence of differently modified classes of ribosomes in normal cells is unknown because no method exists to simultaneously evaluate the modification status at all sites within a single rRNA molecule.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in existing methodology that motivates the study.

claim: The authors developed a reliable method to track the modification status of single rRNA molecules at 37 sites in 18 S rRNA and 73 sites in 25 S rRNA.
source: Using a combination of yeast genetics and nanopore direct RNA sequencing, we developed a reliable method to track the modification status of single rRNA molecules at 37 sites in 18 S rRNA and 73 sites in 25 S rRNA.
evidence: This is the primary methodological claim of the paper stated in the abstract.

claim: The method characterizes patterns of modification heterogeneity in rRNA.
source: We use our method to characterize patterns of modification heterogeneity and identify concerted modification of nucleotides found near functional centers of the ribosome.
evidence: This is stated as a result of applying the method.

claim: The method identifies concerted modification of nucleotides found near functional centers of the ribosome.
source: We use our method to characterize patterns of modification heterogeneity and identify concerted modification of nucleotides found near functional centers of the ribosome.
evidence: This is stated as a key finding in the abstract.

claim: Distinct, undermodified subpopulations of rRNAs accumulate upon loss of Dbp3 RNA helicase.
source: Distinct, undermodified subpopulations of rRNAs accumulate upon loss of Dbp3 or Prp43 RNA helicases, suggesting overlapping roles in ribosome biogenesis.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the experiments with helicase mutants.

claim: Distinct, undermodified subpopulations of rRNAs accumulate upon loss of Prp43 RNA helicase.
source: Distinct, undermodified subpopulations of rRNAs accumulate upon loss of Dbp3 or Prp43 RNA helicases, suggesting overlapping roles in ribosome biogenesis.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the experiments with helicase mutants.

claim: Loss of Dbp3 and Prp43 RNA helicases suggests overlapping roles in ribosome biogenesis.
source: Distinct, undermodified subpopulations of rRNAs accumulate upon loss of Dbp3 or Prp43 RNA helicases, suggesting overlapping roles in ribosome biogenesis.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data presented in the abstract.

claim: Modification profiles are surprisingly resistant to change in response to many genetic and acute environmental conditions that affect translation, ribosome biogenesis, and pre-mRNA splicing.
source: Modification profiles are surprisingly resistant to change in response to many genetic and acute environmental conditions that affect translation, ribosome biogenesis, and pre-mRNA splicing.
evidence: This is stated as a key finding in the abstract.

claim: There are more than 160 distinctly modified ribonucleotides found in the RNA and DNA of cells.
source: In addition to the four standard nucleotides, there are more than 160 distinctly modified ribonucleotides and more than 50 distinctly modified deoxyribonucleotides found in the RNA and DNA of cells (Boccaletto et al., 2018; Jonkhout et al., 2017; Sood et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: There are more than 50 distinctly modified deoxyribonucleotides found in the RNA and DNA of cells.
source: In addition to the four standard nucleotides, there are more than 160 distinctly modified ribonucleotides and more than 50 distinctly modified deoxyribonucleotides found in the RNA and DNA of cells (Boccaletto et al., 2018; Jonkhout et al., 2017; Sood et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Irregular DNA methylation patterns are linked to several cancers, neurological disorders and autoimmune diseases.
source: Irregular DNA methylation patterns are linked to several cancers, neurological disorders and autoimmune diseases (Portela and Esteller, 2010; Raiber et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Aberrant RNA modification has been linked to the development of cognitive functions, neurological defects, breast cancer, genetic birth defects, and diabetes.
source: Aberrant RNA modification has been linked to the development of cognitive functions, neurological defects, breast cancer, genetic birth defects, and diabetes (Bednářová et al., 2017; Benrahma et al., 2014; Delaunay et al., 2016; Delaunay and Frye, 2019; Hideyama et al., 2012; Wu et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: In ribosomal RNA (rRNA), extensive and highly conserved modifications are vital for correct ribosome structure and function.
source: In ribosomal RNA (rRNA), extensive and highly conserved modifications are vital for correct ribosome structure and function (Polikanov et al., 2015; Sloan et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Modifications on rRNA have been generally considered to be constitutive in support of fine tuning function rather than mediating specific regulatory changes in ribosome function.
source: Modifications on rRNA have been generally considered to be constitutive in support of fine tuning function (Karijolich et al., 2010) rather than mediating specific regulatory changes in ribosome function.
evidence: This is cited from published literature as a prevailing view.

claim: The fraction of rRNA molecules modified at individual positions can change in response to the environment, disease and developmental state.
source: However, the fraction of rRNA molecules modified at individual positions can change in response to the environment, disease and developmental state (Birkedal et al., 2015; Sloan et al., 2017; Taoka et al., 2016), and evidence is accumulating that ribosome heterogeneity may influence translation (Gay et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2021b).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Evidence is accumulating that ribosome heterogeneity may influence translation.
source: However, the fraction of rRNA molecules modified at individual positions can change in response to the environment, disease and developmental state (Birkedal et al., 2015; Sloan et al., 2017; Taoka et al., 2016), and evidence is accumulating that ribosome heterogeneity may influence translation (Gay et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2021b).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: It seems possible that modification status throughout locations in the ribosome could control translation by creating functional heterogeneity in the cell's pool of ribosomes.
source: It seems possible that modification status throughout locations in the ribosome could control translation by creating functional heterogeneity in the cell's pool of ribosomes.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis or speculation based on the cited evidence.

claim: No method is available to capture the modification state at all positions of a single RNA molecule.
source: One technical challenge of analyzing the effect of modification on the function of RNA is that no method is available to capture the modification state at all positions of a single RNA molecule.
evidence: This is stated as a technical limitation in the field.

claim: Traditional approaches examine ensembles of molecules and estimate the fraction modified at individual sites independently.
source: Traditional approaches examine ensembles of molecules and estimate the fraction modified at individual sites independently.
evidence: This is stated as a description of existing methods.

claim: Liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) can identify the presence of all types of modified nucleotides in ensembles of rRNA molecules.
source: For example, non-sequencing based techniques such as liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) (Taoka et al., 2009) and cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) (Natchiar et al., 2017) can identify the presence of all types of modified nucleotides in ensembles of rRNA molecules.
evidence: This is cited from published literature describing existing methods.

claim: Cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) can identify the presence of all types of modified nucleotides in ensembles of rRNA molecules.
source: For example, non-sequencing based techniques such as liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) (Taoka et al., 2009) and cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) (Natchiar et al., 2017) can identify the presence of all types of modified nucleotides in ensembles of rRNA molecules.
evidence: This is cited from published literature describing existing methods.

claim: Some methods such as immunoprecipitation-seq aggregate information from several reads to detect modifications at a specific site, but do not capture associations between modification status at distant sites in large RNA molecules.
source: Some methods such as immunoprecipitation-seq (Dominissini et al., 2012) or mismatch-seq (Ramaswami et al., 2013), aggregate information from several reads to detect modifications at a specific site, but do not capture associations between modification status at distant sites in large RNA molecules.
evidence: This is cited from published literature describing limitations of existing methods.

claim: Approaches such as bisulfite-seq, Ψ-seq, and RiboMeth-seq are highly specific for a single type of modified nucleotide, but require fragmentation of RNA, preventing capture of modification status at multiple distant sites in an RNA.
source: Other approaches such as bisulfite-seq (Frommer et al., 1992), Ψ-seq ('psi-seq') (Schwartz et al., 2014), and RiboMeth-seq (Birkedal et al., 2015) are highly specific for a single type of modified nucleotide, but also require fragmentation of RNA, preventing capture of modification status at multiple distant sites in an RNA.
evidence: This is cited from published literature describing limitations of existing methods.

claim: Direct nanopore sequencing of full-length RNA molecules has the potential to report modification status across entire RNA molecules without chemical treatment or amplification steps.
source: Direct nanopore sequencing of full-length RNA molecules (Deamer et al., 2016; Garalde et al., 2016) has the potential to report modification status across entire RNA molecules without chemical treatment or amplification steps.
evidence: This is cited from published literature describing the potential of nanopore sequencing.

claim: Modified nucleotides produce changes in electrical current distinct from canonical nucleotides in nanopore sequencing.
source: Modified nucleotides produce changes in electrical current distinct from canonical nucleotides, permitting modification detection algorithms to identify modifications in both DNA and RNA.
evidence: This is stated as a principle of nanopore sequencing technology.

claim: No currently available method captures combinations of distinctly modified nucleotides at multiple distant sites in RNA.
source: However, no currently available method captures combinations of distinctly modified nucleotides at multiple distant sites in RNA.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in existing methods that the study addresses.

claim: The authors demonstrate accurate, single molecule modification profiling of 13 distinct types of modified nucleotides at 110 positions across full transcripts of 18 S and 25 S rRNA from S. cerevisiae.
source: Here, we demonstrate accurate, single molecule modification profiling of 13 distinct types of modified nucleotides at 110 positions across full transcripts of 18 S and 25 S rRNA from S. cerevisiae.
evidence: This is stated as a key result of the study.

claim: The method preserves long-range associations between modification status at distant positions on single RNA molecules.
source: We preserve long-range associations between modification status at distant positions on single RNA molecules, allowing us to identify highly correlated positions and explore heterogeneity in ribosomal RNA modification.
evidence: This is stated as a key capability of the method.

claim: Clustering analysis separates populations of distinctly modified ribosomes in wild type yeast.
source: Clustering analysis separates populations of distinctly modified ribosomes in wild type yeast, as well as in yeast deficient in gene functions required for modification including Cbf5, Nop58, several snoRNAs, RNA helicases Dbp3, Prp43, and their G-patch protein partners.
evidence: This is stated as a result of applying the method.

claim: Clustering analysis separates populations of distinctly modified ribosomes in yeast deficient in Cbf5.
source: Clustering analysis separates populations of distinctly modified ribosomes in wild type yeast, as well as in yeast deficient in gene functions required for modification including Cbf5, Nop58, several snoRNAs, RNA helicases Dbp3, Prp43, and their G-patch protein partners.
evidence: This is stated as a result of applying the method.

claim: Clustering analysis separates populations of distinctly modified ribosomes in yeast deficient in Nop58.
source: Clustering analysis separates populations of distinctly modified ribosomes in wild type yeast, as well as in yeast deficient in gene functions required for modification including Cbf5, Nop58, several snoRNAs, RNA helicases Dbp3, Prp43, and their G-patch protein partners.
evidence: This is stated as a result of applying the method.

claim: Clustering analysis separates populations of distinctly modified ribosomes in yeast deficient in several snoRNAs.
source: Clustering analysis separates populations of distinctly modified ribosomes in wild type yeast, as well as in yeast deficient in gene functions required for modification including Cbf5, Nop58, several snoRNAs, RNA helicases Dbp3, Prp43, and their G-patch protein partners.
evidence: This is stated as a result of applying the method.

claim: Clustering analysis separates populations of distinctly modified ribosomes in yeast deficient in RNA helicase Dbp3.
source: Clustering analysis separates populations of distinctly modified ribosomes in wild type yeast, as well as in yeast deficient in gene functions required for modification including Cbf5, Nop58, several snoRNAs, RNA helicases Dbp3, Prp43, and their G-patch protein partners.
evidence: This is stated as a result of applying the method.

claim: Clustering analysis separates populations of distinctly modified ribosomes in yeast deficient in RNA helicase Prp43.
source: Clustering analysis separates populations of distinctly modified ribosomes in wild type yeast, as well as in yeast deficient in gene functions required for modification including Cbf5, Nop58, several snoRNAs, RNA helicases Dbp3, Prp43, and their G-patch protein partners.
evidence: This is stated as a result of applying the method.

claim: These studies provide evidence that groups of nucleotides are modified in a concerted manner, especially at functional centers of the ribosome.
source: These studies provide evidence that groups of nucleotides are modified in a concerted manner, especially at functional centers of the ribosome.
evidence: This is stated as a key conclusion of the study.

claim: The authors trained signalAlign by modeling wild type rRNA reads as 'modified' and in vitro transcribed (IVT) reads as 'unmodified' to detect all 110 annotated modifications in S. cerevisiae 18 S and 25 S rRNA.
source: To create these single molecule profiles, we trained signalAlign (Rand et al., 2017) by modeling wild type rRNA reads as 'modified' and in vitro transcribed (IVT) reads as 'unmodified' to detect all 110 annotated modifications in S. cerevisiae 18 S and 25 S rRNA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1 and file supplement 1) (see Materials and methods) (Stoiber et al., 2016; Taoka et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a methodological approach in the Results section.

claim: In S. cerevisiae, 34 of the 37 18 S annotated modifications are guided by the C/D box (2´O-methylation) and H/ACA box (pseudouridylation) snoRNPs.
source: In S. cerevisiae, 34 of the 37 18 S and 66 of the 73 25 S rRNA annotated modifications are guided by the C/D box (2´O-methylation) and H/ACA box (pseudouridylation) snoRNPs (Piekna-Przybylska et al., 2007; Tollervey and Kiss, 1997; Yang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: In S. cerevisiae, 66 of the 73 25 S rRNA annotated modifications are guided by the C/D box (2´O-methylation) and H/ACA box (pseudouridylation) snoRNPs.
source: In S. cerevisiae, 34 of the 37 18 S and 66 of the 73 25 S rRNA annotated modifications are guided by the C/D box (2´O-methylation) and H/ACA box (pseudouridylation) snoRNPs (Piekna-Przybylska et al., 2007; Tollervey and Kiss, 1997; Yang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Single-molecule modification profiles produced by the model reveal accumulation of large numbers of rRNA molecules lacking most 2´O-methyl modifications at snoRNA-guided positions in Nop58-depleted cells.
source: Under these conditions, single-molecule modification profiles produced by our model reveal accumulation of large numbers of rRNA molecules lacking most 2´O-methyl (Nm) (Nop58-depleted) or pseudouridine (Ψ) (Cbf5-depleted) modifications at snoRNA-guided positions in 18 S (Supplementary file 1B Figure 1—figure supplement 3) or 25 S rRNA (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated as a result from the depletion experiments.

claim: Single-molecule modification profiles produced by the model reveal accumulation of large numbers of rRNA molecules lacking most pseudouridine modifications at snoRNA-guided positions in Cbf5-depleted cells.
source: Under these conditions, single-molecule modification profiles produced by our model reveal accumulation of large numbers of rRNA molecules lacking most 2´O-methyl (Nm) (Nop58-depleted) or pseudouridine (Ψ) (Cbf5-depleted) modifications at snoRNA-guided positions in 18 S (Supplementary file 1B Figure 1—figure supplement 3) or 25 S rRNA (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated as a result from the depletion experiments.

claim: Hierarchical clustering of 25 S rRNA modification profiles shows clear separation of subpopulations representing wild type rRNA, IVTs, and molecules arising from the Nop58 or Cbf5-depleted cells.
source: After pooling profiles from the separate samples and clustering them, we observe clear separation of subpopulations representing wild type rRNA, IVTs, and molecules arising from the Nop58 or Cbf5-depleted cells (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 3A).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by Figure 1A.

claim: UMAP visualization of 18 S and 25 S rRNA modification profiles confirms the presence of distinct molecular populations.
source: We used dimension reduction UMAP visualization (McInnes et al., 2018) of 18 S and 25 S rRNA modification profiles to confirm the presence of these distinct molecular populations (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by Figure 1C.

claim: Comparing clusters derived from cells depleted for either of the two different classes snoRNPs shows very little overlap in rRNA modification profiles, suggesting that 2´O methylation and pseudouridylation are largely independent of each other.
source: Comparing clusters 1 and 3 derived from cells depleted for either of the two different classes snoRNPs (Figure 1A and C) shows very little overlap in rRNA modification profiles, suggesting that 2´O methylation and pseudouridylation are largely independent of each other.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the clustering results shown in Figure 1A and C.

claim: Some molecules from snoRNP-depleted cells appear to be modified normally and are found in cluster 2 with wild type rRNA.
source: Some molecules from snoRNP-depleted cells appear to be modified normally and are found in cluster 2 with wild type rRNA (Figure 1A and C), more often for 18 S rRNA than for 25 S rRNA (compare to Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the clustering results.

claim: The presence of normally modified molecules from snoRNP-depleted cells may reflect a more severe impact of modification loss on accumulation of 18 S rRNA, leading to higher residual ribosomes modified before depletion was complete.
source: This may reflect a more severe impact of modification loss on accumulation of 18 S rRNA (Lafontaine et al., 1998; Lafontaine and Tollervey, 1999), leading to higher residual ribosomes modified before depletion was complete.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the observation, citing previous literature.

claim: In the absence of Cbf5 and Nop58, the correlated loss of pseudouridine and 2´O-methyl modifications is highly significant.
source: In the absence of Cbf5 and Nop58, we observe that the correlated loss of pseudouridine (p-value = 5.5e-05, Brown's method) and 2´O-methyl (p-value = 1.5e-16, Brown's method) modifications is highly significant, respectively (Figure 1D and E and Figure 1—figure supplement 3E,F).
evidence: This is stated as a result with statistical support.

claim: A comparison of the pairwise correlation tests for all combinations of modified positions confirmed that to a large extent 2´O-methylation and pseudouridylation in yeast are independent of each other.
source: As suggested by the clustering results, a comparison of the pairwise correlation tests for all combinations of modified positions confirmed that to a large extent 2´O-methylation and pseudouridylation in yeast are independent of each other (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is stated as a result from correlation analysis.

claim: The sites of methylation guided by the C/D box snoRNA U24 (Cm1437, Am1449, and Gm1450) within the polypeptide exit tunnel in 25 S rRNA appear to be modified in a concerted fashion.
source: The sites of methylation guided by the C/D box snoRNA U24 (Cm1437, Am1449, and Gm1450) within the polypeptide exit tunnel (PET) in 25 S rRNA appear to be modified in a concerted fashion.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: Approximately 40% of the molecules from the Nop58 depletion remain methylated at all three U24-guided sites despite being unmethylated at most other sites.
source: Approximately 40% of the molecules from the Nop58 depletion remain methylated at all three sites despite being unmethylated at most other sites, (Figure 1A), suggesting that either the modification of this triad is more efficient, or that rRNAs lacking these modifications are more unstable.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from Figure 1A with interpretation.

claim: About 13% of molecules in the cluster formed by depletion of the pseudouridylase Cbf5 are also unmethylated at all three U24-guided sites.
source: Furthermore, about 13% of molecules in the cluster formed by depletion of the pseudouridylase Cbf5 are also unmethylated at all three sites, suggesting that concerted methylation at these positions may be partly dependent on pseudouridine modification.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with interpretation.

claim: The highly concerted modification between 25 S rRNA positions Um2921, Gm2922, and Ψ2923 in the peptidyl transfer center appears refractory to loss of modification in both depletion experiments.
source: Particularly striking is the highly concerted modification between 25 S rRNA positions Um2921 with Gm2922 and Ψ2923 in the peptidyl transfer center (PTC). These appear refractory to loss of modification in both depletion experiments, remaining modified on a large fraction of molecules otherwise lacking multiple other modifications (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from Figure 1A.

claim: Modification of Um2921 is guided by C/D box snoRNA snR52.
source: Modification of Um2921 is guided by C/D box snoRNA snR52, and Gm2922 is modified by the non-snoRNP methyltransferase Spb1, which can also methylate Um2921 in the absence of snR52 (Lapeyre and Purushothaman, 2004).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Gm2922 is modified by the non-snoRNP methyltransferase Spb1, which can also methylate Um2921 in the absence of snR52.
source: Modification of Um2921 is guided by C/D box snoRNA snR52, and Gm2922 is modified by the non-snoRNP methyltransferase Spb1, which can also methylate Um2921 in the absence of snR52 (Lapeyre and Purushothaman, 2004).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Methylation of G2922 appears to be critically required for maturation and nuclear export of the pre-60S ribosomal subunit.
source: Consistent with this, methylation of G2922 appears to be critically required for maturation and nuclear export of the pre-60S ribosomal subunit (Yelland et al., 2022).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Modification of Ψ2923 does not have a known redundant snoRNP or enzymatic backup mechanism for modification in the absence of snR10.
source: However, modification of Ψ2923 does not have a known redundant snoRNP or enzymatic backup mechanism for modification in the absence of snR10.
evidence: This is stated as a fact about the modification pathway.

claim: The extremely low number of observed molecules lacking modification at Um2921, Gm2922, and Ψ2923 suggests that rRNAs do not accumulate efficiently in their absence.
source: Thus, the extremely low number of observed molecules lacking modification at these important positions suggests that rRNAs do not accumulate efficiently in their absence.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the observation.

claim: A concerted change in loss of modification is observed between the two N4-acetylcytidines (ac4C1280 and ac4C1773) in 18 S, and loss of 2´O-methylation at many positions in the Nop58 depletion.
source: We also observe a concerted change in loss of modification between the two N4-acetylcytidines (ac4C1280 and ac4C1773) in 18 S, and loss of 2´O-methylation at many positions in the Nop58 depletion (P-value = 2.3e-05, Brown's method) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,E).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with statistical support.

claim: N4-acetylcytidine modification depends on the C/D box snoRNAs snR4 and snR45, which bring the cytidine acetylase Kre33 to positions C1280 and C1773, respectively.
source: N4-acetylcytidine modification depends on the C/D box snoRNAs snR4 and snR45, which are not known to guide methylation, but instead bring the cytidine acetylase Kre33 to positions C1280 and C1773, respectively (Sharma et al., 2017; van Nues et al., 2011).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: These atypical C/D box snRNAs also require Nop58, explaining the coordinate loss of cytidine acetylation and 2´O-methylation.
source: These atypical C/D box snRNAs also require Nop58, explaining the coordinate loss of cytidine acetylation and 2´O-methylation.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for the observed correlation.

claim: The model recognizes ac4C modified sites, as confirmed by knocking out snR4 and snR45 and observing loss of the expected N4-acetylcytidine.
source: We confirmed that our model recognizes ac4C modified sites by knocking out snR4 and snR45 and observing loss of the expected N4-acetylcytidine (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated as a validation experiment.

claim: The N1-methyl-N3-aminocarboxypropyl-pseudouridine (m1acp3Ψ1191) residue in 18 S is significantly correlated with pseudouridine positions in the Cbf5 depletion.
source: Also, the N1-methyl-N3-aminocarboxypropyl-pseudouridine (m1acp3Ψ1191) residue in 18 S is significantly correlated with pseudouridine positions in the Cbf5 depletion (p-value = 5.4e-07, Brown's method) (Figure 1—figure supplement 3A,F), as expected given that snR35-guided pseudouridylation of U1191 is the first step to generate this complex modification (Brand et al., 1978).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with statistical support and cited explanation.

claim: The concerted pattern of modifications predicted by the model agree with the underlying event means clustering, with the exception that modification of Ψ2923 may be slightly overestimated.
source: This test reveals that the concerted pattern of modifications predicted by the model agree with the underlying event means clustering, with the exception that modification of Ψ2923 may be slightly overestimated (Figure 1—figure supplement 4 and note supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as a result from validation analysis.

claim: Based on the largest variance (position 562 in 18 S, ~ 9%), a conservative cutoff of a 10% change in modification was chosen to call any site affected by a given experimental perturbation.
source: Based on the largest variance (position 562 in 18 S, ~ 9%), we chose a conservative cutoff of a 10% change in modification to call any site affected by a given experimental perturbation (mutation or treatment, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as a methodological decision based on data.

claim: Sequencing rRNAs from strains containing individual snoRNA knockouts (snR80, snR83, snR87, snR4, and snR45) demonstrated significant decreases in modification at the appropriate site for each.
source: We sequenced rRNAs from strains containing individual snoRNA knockouts (snR80, snR83, snR87, snR4, and snR45) previously shown to completely lack modification at one or a few annotated sites in each case (Piekna-Przybylska et al., 2007), demonstrating significant decreases in modification at the appropriate site for each (p-values < 1e-04, chi-square test) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and E).
evidence: This is stated as a validation result with statistical support.

claim: Signal distributions from snoRNA knockout kmers match the model's canonical unmodified kmer distributions.
source: As expected, signal distributions from snoRNA knockout kmers match the model's canonical unmodified kmer distributions (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as a validation result.

claim: Hierarchical clustering of the profiles obtained from the mixture of three snoRNA knockout strains and wild type reveals four similarly sized main clusters of differently modified 18 S rRNA.
source: Hierarchical clustering of the profiles obtained from the mixture reveals four similarly sized main clusters of differently modified 18 S rRNA (Figure 2A and C) (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated as a result from the mixture experiment.

claim: Positive correlation changes are observed between positions Ψ1290 and Ψ1415 in the mixture experiment, likely arising from their shared dependence on snR83.
source: We observe positive correlation changes between positions Ψ1290 and Ψ1415 (Figure 2B) (p-value = 6.4e-16, Fisher z-transform test), that likely arise from their shared dependence on snR83.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with statistical support and interpretation.

claim: Negative correlation changes are observed between all independent pairs of modification sites at Am436, Ψ759, and [Ψ1290+Ψ1415] only in the artificial mixture.
source: Moreover, we observe negative correlation changes between all independent pairs of modification sites at Am436, Ψ759, and [Ψ1290+Ψ1415] only in the artificial mixture (Figure 2B and Supplementary file 1A) (p-value = 3.5e-08, Brown's method).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with statistical support.

claim: The population in the mixture would be extremely unlikely to have molecules with simultaneous loss of modification at any pair of Am436, Ψ759, and [Ψ1290+Ψ1415] locations, creating the negative correlation change.
source: Since loss of modification at these positions in this test mixture arose independently in the separate samples that were mixed, the population would be extremely unlikely to have molecules with simultaneous loss of modification at any pair of these three locations, creating the negative correlation change.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for the observed negative correlation.

claim: By ensemble methods, most rRNA positions are almost completely ( > 95%) modified and cluster around functional centers, with a few that are partially modified.
source: By ensemble methods, most rRNA positions are almost completely ( > 95%) modified and cluster around functional centers, with a few that are partially modified (Figure 1—figure supplement 5; Birkedal et al., 2015; Marchand et al., 2016; Taoka et al., 2016; Yang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from published literature and shown in a figure.

claim: The model arrives at very similar estimates to ensemble methods when taken one position at a time.
source: Taken one position at a time, our model arrives at very similar estimates (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison result shown in a figure.

claim: Hierarchical clustering of wild type profiles shows no large classes of distinctly modified ribosomes.
source: Hierarchical clustering of wild type profiles shows no large classes of distinctly modified ribosomes.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from clustering analysis.

claim: Some smaller ( < 10% of total) subpopulations are apparent in wild type that have correlated pairs of unmodified nucleotides.
source: However, some smaller ( < 10% of total) subpopulations are apparent that have correlated pairs of unmodified nucleotides (Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 5A), confirmed by comparing wild type to IVT (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 5B) (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from clustering analysis.

claim: One pair of significantly correlated positions in 18 S, Ψ632 and Ψ766, are guided by the same snoRNA, snR161, likely explaining the basis for this correlation.
source: One pair of significantly correlated positions in 18 S, Ψ632 and Ψ766 (p-value = 1.3e-04, Fisher z-transform test) are guided by the same snoRNA, snR161, likely explaining the basis for this correlation.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with statistical support and interpretation.

claim: A significant correlation is observed between Am100 and Am436 in 18 S wild type.
source: We observe a significant correlation between Am100 and Am436 (p-value = 3.1e-04, Fisher z-transform test) as well as between Cm1639 and ac4C1773 in 18 S (p-value = 4.5e-06, Fisher z-transform test) (Figure 2F), neither of which share a snoRNA or modification enzyme.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with statistical support.

claim: A significant correlation is observed between Cm1639 and ac4C1773 in 18 S wild type.
source: We observe a significant correlation between Am100 and Am436 (p-value = 3.1e-04, Fisher z-transform test) as well as between Cm1639 and ac4C1773 in 18 S (p-value = 4.5e-06, Fisher z-transform test) (Figure 2F), neither of which share a snoRNA or modification enzyme.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with statistical support.

claim: Cm1639 (snR70) in the P-site is correlated with Ψ999 (snR31, E-site) in 18 S wild type.
source: Cm1639 (snR70) in the P-site is also correlated with Ψ999 (snR31, E-site, p-value = 1.7e-03, Fisher z-transform test), and ac4C1280 (Kre33, P-value = 3.9e-05, Fisher z-transform test) (Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with statistical support.

claim: Cm1639 is correlated with ac4C1280 in 18 S wild type.
source: Cm1639 (snR70) in the P-site is also correlated with Ψ999 (snR31, E-site, p-value = 1.7e-03, Fisher z-transform test), and ac4C1280 (Kre33, P-value = 3.9e-05, Fisher z-transform test) (Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with statistical support.

claim: ac4C1773 and m26A1782 (Dim1, intersubunit bridge) are correlated in 18 S wild type.
source: Furthermore, ac4C1773 and m26A1782 (Dim1, intersubunit bridge, p-value = 1.7e-04, Fisher z-transform test) are correlated.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with statistical support.

claim: Some correlated pairs lie close to each other (15–22 Å) in the three-dimensional structure of the mature ribosome, suggesting a structural or functional basis for their coordinate modification status.
source: Some correlated pairs lie close to each other (15–22 Å) in the three-dimensional structure of the mature ribosome (Figure 2G), suggesting a structural or functional basis for their coordinate modification status.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with interpretation based on structural data.

claim: In 25 S, the three U24-guided positions Cm1437, Am1449, and Gm1450 are all significantly more correlated with each other than expected in wild type.
source: In 25 S, the three U24-guided positions Cm1437, Am1449, and Gm1450 are all significantly more correlated with each other than expected (p-value = 1.0e-44, Brown's method) (Figure 2—figure supplement 5), echoing our observations in the depletion experiment.
evidence: This is stated as an observation with statistical support.

claim: Compared to wild-type control strains at 30 °C or 18 °C, loss of 2´O methylation at specific locations in 18 S and 25 S rRNAs is observed in the Dbp3 knockout strain (dbp3ᐃ) or the cold-sensitive Prp43 Q423N mutant (prp43-cs) grown at nonpermissive temperature.
source: Compared to wild-type control strains at 30 °C or 18 °C, we observe loss of 2´O methylation at specific locations in 18 S and 25 S rRNAs in the Dbp3 knockout strain (dbp3ᐃ) or the cold-sensitive Prp43 Q423N mutant (prp43-cs) grown at nonpermissive temperature (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplements 1–3) consistent with previous ensemble studies (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C, D; Aquino et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as an observation consistent with previous studies.

claim: Hierarchical clustering of 25 S rRNA single-molecule profiles reveals that just 2–3 distinct but related sets of modification profiles describe nearly all ribosomes in both dbp3ᐃ and prp43-cs experiments.
source: Despite the numerous locations at which modification is compromised, hierarchical clustering of 25 S rRNA single-molecule profiles reveals that just 2–3 distinct but related sets of modification profiles describe nearly all ribosomes in both experiments (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated as a result from clustering analysis.

claim: The triad of 2´O methylations guided by the snoRNA U24 at 25 S positions 1437, 1449, and 1450 surrounding the PET are often left unmodified in a highly concerted manner in dbp3ᐃ and prp43-cs mutants.
source: The triad of 2´O methylations guided by the snoRNA U24 at 25 S positions 1437, 1449, and 1450 surrounding the PET are often left unmodified in a highly concerted manner (Figure 3B), as observed in a minority of wild type 25 S rRNA molecules (Figure 2—figure supplement 5), and in the snoRNP depletion experiments (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: The pairwise correlations within the U24-guided triad are significantly higher in both the dbp3ᐃ and the prp43-cs mutants relative to wild type.
source: The pairwise correlations within this triad are significantly higher in both the dbp3ᐃ and the prp43-cs mutants relative to wild type (dbp3ᐃ p-value = 3.6e-68, prp43-cs 3.5e-11, Brown's method) (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1D, E).
evidence: This is stated as a result with statistical support.

claim: Clustering the underlying raw signal event means from the dbp3ᐃ and prp43-cs mutants reveals two clear subpopulations of reads distinguished by the signal means at positions C1437, A1449, and G1450.
source: To confirm the highly concerted modification of the closely spaced U24-dependent positions, we clustered the underlying raw signal event means from the dbp3ᐃ and prp43-cs mutants as above (see Materials and methods) (Ding et al., 2020). This reveals two clear subpopulations of reads distinguished by the signal means at positions C1437, A1449, and G1450 in both the dbp3ᐃ and prp43-cs mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated as a validation result.

claim: If the U24 snoRNP is unable to guide modification of any of the positions C1437, A1449, or G1450, then all 3 positions are left unmodified.
source: Therefore, if the U24 snoRNP is unable to guide modification of any of these positions, then all 3 positions are left unmodified.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the clustering results.

claim: Both Dbp3 and Prp43 functions are required for the concerted modification of nucleotides near the PET.
source: Furthermore, both Dbp3 and Prp43 functions are required for the concerted modification of these nucleotides near the PET.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Deletion of Sqs1 had little effect on modification.
source: Although deletion of Sqs1 had little effect on modification (see below), loss of Pxr1 produced modification profiles similar to the prp43-cs mutant, but with more extreme modification deficiencies (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: Loss of Pxr1 produced modification profiles similar to the prp43-cs mutant, but with more extreme modification deficiencies.
source: Although deletion of Sqs1 had little effect on modification (see below), loss of Pxr1 produced modification profiles similar to the prp43-cs mutant, but with more extreme modification deficiencies (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: All modifications affected by prp43-cs and all but two 18 S 2´O methylations affected by dbp3ᐃ are also affected in pxr1ᐃ.
source: All modifications affected by prp43-cs and all but two 18 S 2´O methylations affected by dbp3ᐃ (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) are also affected in pxr1ᐃ.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: Loss of Prp43 activity guided by Pxr1, but not that guided by Sqs1, is responsible for the concerted changes in modification pattern observed in the prp43-cs strain.
source: This suggests that loss of Prp43 activity guided by Pxr1, but not that guided by Sqs1, is responsible for the concerted changes in modification pattern observed in the prp43-cs strain.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the data.

claim: In 25 S, positions Am817 and Gm908 (both guided by snR60) and Gm2619 and Um2724 (both guided by snR67) are significantly more correlated in both pxr1ᐃ and dbp3ᐃ relative to wild type.
source: For example, in 25 S, positions Am817 and Gm908 (both guided by snR60) and Gm2619 and Um2724 (both guided by snR67) are significantly more correlated in both pxr1ᐃ and dbp3ᐃ relative to wild type (817–908 p-value = 4.7e-17 and 2.4e-33, 2619–2724 p-value = 7.2 e-04 and 3.5e-22, Fisher z-transform tests) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with statistical support.

claim: Positions Am817 and Gm908, and Gm2619 and Um2724 are not significantly more correlated in the prp43-cs mutant relative to wild type.
source: However, they are not significantly more correlated in the prp43-cs mutant relative to wild type (817–908 p-value = 0.34, 2619–2724 p-value = 0.919, Fisher z-transform test).
evidence: This is stated as an observation with statistical support.

claim: Pxr1 and Dbp3 both appear to promote concerted modification of positions guided by snR60 and snR67.
source: Pxr1 and Dbp3 both appear to promote concerted modification of positions guided by snR60 and snR67; however, the contribution of Prp43 is less clear.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the data.

claim: It is possible that the conditional Prp43 mutation is not severe enough to produce a strong block to modification at snR60 and snR67 sites, or alternatively that Pxr1 has functions in addition to its role in support of Prp43.
source: It is possible that the conditional Prp43 mutation is not severe enough to produce a strong block to modification at those sites, or alternatively that Pxr1 has functions in addition to its role in support of Prp43.
evidence: This is stated as speculation about the interpretation.

claim: Loss of Prp43 and Pxr1 induce a concerted loss of modification of a set of nucleotides in the decoding site of the small subunit.
source: For example, loss of Prp43 and Pxr1 induce a concerted loss of modification of a set of nucleotides in the decoding site of the small subunit (green circles, Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Loss of Pxr1 leads to concerted loss of a set of modifications in the peptidyl transfer center of the large subunit.
source: Loss of Pxr1 leads to concerted loss of a set of modifications in the peptidyl transfer center of the large subunit (blue circles, Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: All three mutants (dbp3ᐃ, prp43-cs, pxr1ᐃ) create a complex set of correlated modification changes in the triad Cm1437, Am1449, and Gm1450 near the protein exit tunnel of the large subunit.
source: And all three mutants create a complex set of correlated modification changes in the triad Cm1437, Am1449, and Gm1450 near the protein exit tunnel of the large subunit (purple circles, Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Using the threshold of >10% change in modification relative to wild type, splicing-related perturbations were examined for effects on rRNA modification that might be mediated through loss of one or more intronic snoRNAs.
source: Using the threshold of >10% change in modification relative to wild type established above (Figure 1—figure supplement 4 and Figure 3A), we examined splicing-related perturbations for effects on rRNA modification that might be mediated through loss of one or more intronic snoRNAs (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated as a methodological approach.

claim: A 36.8% reduction in modification for 18 S Ψ106 (guided by snR44 from intron 2 of RPS22B) is observed as a consequence of the loss of Dbr1.
source: We observe a 36.8% reduction in modification for 18 S Ψ106 (guided by snR44 from intron 2 of RPS22B) and an 11.0% reduction in modification frequency for 18 S Am974 (guided by snR54 from intron 1 of IMD4) as a consequence of the loss of Dbr1.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: An 11.0% reduction in modification frequency for 18 S Am974 (guided by snR54 from intron 1 of IMD4) is observed as a consequence of the loss of Dbr1.
source: We observe a 36.8% reduction in modification for 18 S Ψ106 (guided by snR44 from intron 2 of RPS22B) and an 11.0% reduction in modification frequency for 18 S Am974 (guided by snR54 from intron 1 of IMD4) as a consequence of the loss of Dbr1.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: Neither the prp16-302 nor spp382-1 mutant produced a modification defect that passed the threshold.
source: Neither the prp16-302 nor spp382-1 mutant produced a modification defect that passed the threshold (Figure 5), suggesting that deficiencies in ongoing splicing do not create noticeable changes in rRNA modification pattern.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: Deficiencies in ongoing splicing do not create noticeable changes in rRNA modification pattern.
source: Neither the prp16-302 nor spp382-1 mutant produced a modification defect that passed the threshold (Figure 5), suggesting that deficiencies in ongoing splicing do not create noticeable changes in rRNA modification pattern.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the observation.

claim: The modification defects observed for prp43-cs arise primarily from its deficiencies in promoting ribosome biogenesis, and not from the loss of its contributions to splicing.
source: These results argue that the modification defects observed for prp43-cs arise primarily from its deficiencies in promoting ribosome biogenesis, and not from the loss of its contributions to splicing.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the splicing experiments.

claim: In none of the environmental treatments tested did the authors detect substantial changes in modification profile.
source: In none of these treatments did we detect substantial changes in modification profile (Figure 5 and Supplementary file 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated as a result from the environmental treatment experiments.

claim: Most annotated modification patterns on rRNA are refractory to rapid alterations by dramatic changes in the physiological conditions tested.
source: Together, these observations indicate that most annotated modification patterns on rRNA are refractory to rapid alterations by dramatic changes in the physiological conditions we tested.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the environmental treatment experiments.

claim: In the case of environmental treatments for 1 hr, cell numbers increased by approximately 1.2–2.4 fold, providing opportunity for new, differently modified ribosomes to be synthesized and detected.
source: In the case of environmental treatments for 1 hr, cell numbers increased by approximately 1.2–2.4 fold, providing opportunity for new, differently modified ribosomes to be synthesized and detected in our experiments.
evidence: This is stated as an observation about the experimental conditions.

claim: The conditions tested are not known to trigger loss of snoRNPs.
source: The conditions we tested are not known to trigger loss of snoRNPs, therefore any rapid changes in modification that might have been observable would have had to rely on either repressing snoRNP function or activation of enzymes that reverse the modification at pre-existing modified sites.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge about the experimental conditions.

claim: At this time, there are no known mechanisms for repressing snoRNP function or enzymes that would reverse either pseudouridylation or 2´O methylation of ribose in RNA.
source: At this time, there are no known mechanisms for repressing snoRNP function or enzymes that would reverse either pseudouridylation or 2´O methylation of ribose in RNA.
evidence: This is stated as current knowledge in the field.

claim: These results do not exclude the possibility that chronic genetic or environmental conditions might alter rRNA modification and ribosome function over the long term.
source: However, these results do not exclude the possibility that chronic genetic or environmental conditions might alter rRNA modification and ribosome function over the long term.
evidence: This is stated as a caveat to the interpretation.

claim: By depletion of the two main classes of snoRNPs responsible for the bulk of rRNA pseudouridylation and 2´O methylation, the authors validated the framework for their method and found that these two classes of snoRNP-dependent modification are largely independent of each other.
source: By depletion of the two main classes of snoRNPs responsible for the bulk of rRNA pseudouridylation and 2´O methylation, we validated the framework for our method and found that these two classes of snoRNP-dependent modification are largely independent of each other (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated as a summary of results in the Discussion.

claim: The authors resolved populations of ribosomes that differ by a single modification, and identified instances of concerted modification of sets of nucleotides in the wild type ribosome population.
source: We resolved populations of ribosomes that differ by a single modification, and identified instances of concerted modification of sets of nucleotides in the wild type ribosome population (Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated as a summary of results in the Discussion.

claim: Analysis of the single molecule modification profiles resulting from loss of two distinct helicase activities provided by Dbp3 and Prp43 (and its G-patch protein Pxr1) reveals a complex set of long-range concerted effects on modification, with implications for ribosome biogenesis and function.
source: Analysis of the single molecule modification profiles resulting from loss of two distinct helicase activities provided by Dbp3 and Prp43 (and its G-patch protein Pxr1) reveals a complex set of long-range concerted effects on modification, with implications for ribosome biogenesis and function (Figures 3, 4 and 6).
evidence: This is stated as a summary of results in the Discussion.

claim: The three nucleotides Cm1437, Am1449, and Gm1450 line the PET, where interactions with the nascent polypeptide chain can influence protein folding, within a few angstroms of conserved loops of ribosomal proteins uL4 (rpL4) and uL22 (rpL17).
source: These three nucleotides line the PET, where interactions with the nascent polypeptide chain can influence protein folding (Choi et al., 2018), within a few angstroms of conserved loops of ribosomal proteins uL4 (rpL4) and uL22 (rpL17) (Ben-Shem et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation cited from published literature.

claim: The conserved loops of uL4 and uL22 insert into the PET to form the constriction site and may act as an 'exit gate'.
source: These protein loops insert into the PET to form the constriction site and may act as an 'exit gate' (Figure 6A and B; Nakatogawa and Ito, 2002; Wilson et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation cited from published literature.

claim: The three positions Cm1437, Am1449, and Gm1450 are in domain 0 of ribosomal rRNA, which acts as a central hub around which the other six 25 S rRNA domains fold.
source: Furthermore, these three positions are in domain 0 of ribosomal rRNA, which acts as a central hub around which the other six 25 S rRNA domains fold (Klinge and Woolford, 2019; Petrov et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a structural observation cited from published literature.

claim: In the absence of Cm1437, Am1449, and Gm1450, the rRNA and the loops of uL4 and uL22 may not be properly positioned, affecting the structure and chemistry of the PET, translation, and protein folding.
source: In the absence of Cm1437, Am1449, and Gm1450, the rRNA and the loops of uL4 and uL22 may not be properly positioned, affecting the structure and chemistry of the PET, translation, and protein folding.
evidence: This is stated as speculation about the functional consequences.

claim: At least 21 putative RNA helicases drive yeast ribosome biogenesis forward by enabling pre-rRNA rearrangements and releasing snoRNPs.
source: At least 21 putative RNA helicases drive yeast ribosome biogenesis forward by enabling pre-rRNA rearrangements and releasing snoRNPs (Martin et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Recent work supports a model in which Dbp3 and Prp43 release certain snoRNPs to allow subsequent modification of adjacent sites by a second snoRNP.
source: Recent work (Aquino et al., 2021) supports a model in which Dbp3 and Prp43 release certain snoRNPs to allow subsequent modification of adjacent sites by a second snoRNP.
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: The authors identify concerted changes in modifications over much longer distances in rRNA when the activity of Dbp3 or Prp43 is compromised, suggesting the regulation of these helicases is important for modifications separated by large stretches of sequence.
source: Here, we identify concerted changes in modifications over much longer distances in rRNA when the activity of Dbp3 or Prp43 is compromised, suggesting the regulation of these helicases is not only important for locally overlapping modified positions, but also for modifications separated by large stretches of sequence (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplements 1–3).
evidence: This is stated as a key finding of the study.

claim: Pxr1, but not Sqs1, is the main G-patch protein important for Prp43 function during rRNA modification.
source: Furthermore, our work shows that Pxr1, but not Sqs1, is the main G-patch protein important for Prp43 function during rRNA modification.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experiments.

claim: Previous work showed that when Prp43 is absent from pre-ribosomes, the snR55 snoRNP is retained on pre-ribosomes but its target site 18 S rRNA Um1269 remains modified.
source: Previous work (Aquino et al., 2021; Bohnsack et al., 2009) showed that when Prp43 is absent from pre-ribosomes, the snR55 snoRNP is retained on pre-ribosomes but its target site 18 S rRNA Um1269 remains modified.
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: This suggests snR55 can bind and direct modification, but then is not efficiently released from the pre-ribosome.
source: This suggests snR55 can bind and direct modification, but then is not efficiently released from the pre-ribosome.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of cited work.

claim: The Prp43-Q423N protein is more tightly associated with snR55 and other snoRNAs than wild type Prp43.
source: Consistent with this, the Prp43-Q423N protein is more tightly associated with snR55 and other snoRNAs than wild type Prp43 (Leeds et al., 2006).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: The Prp43-Q423N mutant protein permits modification of Um1269 by snR55, but causes concerted loss of modification at nucleotides that surround the Prp43 binding site in the base of helix 44.
source: Here we show that the Prp43-Q423N mutant protein permits modification of Um1269 by snR55, but causes concerted loss of modification at nucleotides that surround the Prp43 binding site in the base of helix 44, which appear to be secondary to snR55 modification (Figure 6C; Bohnsack et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as a finding of the study.

claim: Detectable snR55 is associated with pre-ribosomes in the absence of Dbp3, but its ability to modify U1269 is blocked.
source: Detectable snR55 is associated with pre-ribosomes in the absence of Dbp3, but its ability to modify U1269 is blocked (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A; Aquino et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as an observation citing previous work.

claim: The authors propose a hierarchical model for the action of Dbp3 and Prp43/Pxr1 during co-transcriptional ribosome biogenesis.
source: Together, this suggests a hierarchical model for the action of Dbp3 and Prp43/Pxr1 during co-transcriptional ribosome biogenesis (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated as a proposed model based on the data.

claim: Modifications at 5' end of 18 S occur early and co-transcriptionally, independently of later modifications.
source: We propose that modifications at 5' end of 18 S occur early and co-transcriptionally, independently of later modifications.
evidence: This is stated as part of the proposed model.

claim: As transcription and ribosome assembly progresses, Dbp3 becomes necessary for methylation of U1269 by snR55 in 18 S, possibly by promoting a conformational change in the pre-ribosome or snR55.
source: As transcription and ribosome assembly progresses, Dbp3 becomes necessary for methylation of U1269 by snR55 in 18 S, possibly by promoting a conformational change in the pre-ribosome or snR55.
evidence: This is stated as part of the proposed model.

claim: The absence of Dbp3 does not prevent snR55 binding to the pre-ribosome in a fashion that permits modification at positions surrounding the Prp43 binding site.
source: The absence of Dbp3 does not prevent snR55 binding to the pre-ribosome in a fashion that permits modification at positions surrounding the Prp43 binding site (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as part of the proposed model based on data.

claim: After snR55 modification of U1269, Prp43 activity is required for snR55 release, allowing other snoRNPs to modify positions around the Prp43 binding site.
source: However, after snR55 modification of U1269, Prp43 activity is required for snR55 release, allowing other snoRNPs to modify positions around the Prp43 binding site.
evidence: This is stated as part of the proposed model.

claim: Because the Prp43-Q423N protein is slow to dissociate, snR55 and mutant Prp43 are retained on the pre-ribosome, occluding the other snoRNPs, resulting in concerted loss of those modifications.
source: Because the Prp43-Q423N protein is slow to dissociate, snR55 and mutant Prp43 are retained on the pre-ribosome (Bohnsack et al., 2009; Leeds et al., 2006), occluding the other snoRNPs, resulting in concerted loss of those modifications (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: This is stated as part of the proposed model citing previous work.

claim: Prp43 is present in multiple, consecutive pre-ribosomal particles and is thought to bind to different positions along the pre-rRNA.
source: Prp43 is present in multiple, consecutive pre-ribosomal particles and is thought to bind to different positions along the pre-rRNA (Bohnsack et al., 2009; Lebaron et al., 2005), providing opportunity for hierarchical relationships in modification at other locations.
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: During its function in the termination of pre-mRNA splicing, Prp43 is proposed to bind the 3´ end of U6 snRNA and translocate along it, resulting in removal of U6 from the spliceosome.
source: During its function in the termination of pre-mRNA splicing, Prp43 is proposed to bind the 3´ end of U6 snRNA and translocate along it, resulting in removal of U6 from the spliceosome (He et al., 2017; Toroney et al., 2019).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: The authors propose that Prp43 acts in an analogous manner to release certain snoRNPs from the pre-ribosome upon completion of modification.
source: Because many biochemical principles are shared between the spliceosome and the ribosome (Staley and Woolford, 2009), we propose that Prp43 acts in an analogous manner to release certain snoRNPs from the pre-ribosome upon completion of modification.
evidence: This is stated as a proposed model based on analogy.

claim: Hubs of concerted loss of modification in the Prp43 mutant might reflect critical points in ribosome biogenesis where Prp43 removes key snoRNAs.
source: Thus, hubs of concerted loss of modification in the Prp43 mutant might reflect critical points in ribosome biogenesis where Prp43 removes key snoRNAs.
evidence: This is stated as speculation about the interpretation.

claim: The depletion experiments provide clear evidence that most ribosomes are either fully modified or completely unmodified at the three U24-guided sites.
source: The depletion experiments (Figure 1) provide clear evidence that most ribosomes are either fully modified or completely unmodified at those three sites, and the loss of modification in the Dbp3 and Prp43 mutants for this group is similar (Figure 3 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: In yeast, U24 and three other C/D box snoRNPs (U18, snR13, and snR48) are thought to modify 2–3 nucleotides that reside next to each other in sequence.
source: In yeast, U24 and three other C/D box snoRNPs (U18, snR13, and snR48) are thought to modify 2–3 nucleotides that reside next to each other in sequence.
evidence: This is stated as background knowledge.

claim: It has been suggested that alternatively folded forms of the snoRNA within these snoRNPs may guide the individual modifications.
source: It has been suggested that alternatively folded forms of the snoRNA within these snoRNPs may guide the individual modifications (van Nues and Watkins, 2017).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: This proposal and the authors' observations open the possibility of a processive mechanism for concerted local modification events in which one snoRNP binding event with snoRNA refolding in between explains concerted sequential modification dynamics.
source: This proposal and our observations open the possibility of a processive mechanism for concerted local modification events in which one snoRNP binding event with snoRNA refolding in between explains concerted sequential modification dynamics.
evidence: This is stated as speculation based on the data and cited work.

claim: A distributive mechanism would require independent, stochastic snoRNP binding events, as expected for snoRNPs that guide modification of distant sites, or where two different snoRNPs guide closely spaced modified sites.
source: A distributive mechanism would require independent, stochastic snoRNP binding events, as expected for snoRNPs that guide modification of distant sites, or where two different snoRNPs guide closely spaced modified sites.
evidence: This is stated as a description of an alternative mechanism.

claim: The latter case should produce a set of rRNAs with partial modifications in different combinations at these positions, and this is not observed.
source: The latter case should produce a set of rRNAs with partial modifications in different combinations at these positions, and this is not observed (Figures 1 and 3, Figure 2—figure supplement 5, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1), lending weight to the idea that closely spaced modifications guided by a single snoRNP may occur processively.
evidence: This is stated as an observation that supports the processive mechanism hypothesis.

claim: The diameter of a snoRNP may approach 100 Å.
source: The diameter of a snoRNP may approach 100 Å (Duan et al., 2009; Lin et al., 2011), whereas the yeast ribosome is approximately 250 Å in diameter.
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: The yeast ribosome is approximately 250 Å in diameter.
source: The diameter of a snoRNP may approach 100 Å (Duan et al., 2009; Lin et al., 2011), whereas the yeast ribosome is approximately 250 Å in diameter.
evidence: This is stated as a structural fact.

claim: If two different snoRNPs have overlapping binding sites that guide two closely spaced modifications, they almost certainly must act sequentially.
source: Thus, if two different snoRNPs have overlapping binding sites that guide two closely spaced modifications, they almost certainly must act sequentially.
evidence: This is stated as a logical inference from the size constraints.

claim: In this instance, concerted loss of modification could occur if the pre-rRNA substrate fails to adopt a conformation that renders the local region containing both sites accessible.
source: In this instance, concerted loss of modification could occur if the pre-rRNA substrate fails to adopt a conformation that renders the local region containing both sites accessible.
evidence: This is stated as a possible explanation.

claim: If the site is accessible and modification proceeds distributively then intermediates representing partial modification should be observed, in particular under depletion of C/D box snoRNPs or loss of Dbp3.
source: However, if the site is accessible and modification proceeds distributively then intermediates representing partial modification should be observed, in particular under depletion of C/D box snoRNPs (Figure 1) or loss of Dbp3 (Figure 3; Aquino et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as a prediction of the distributive model.

claim: Two main populations of ribosomes are observed at the U24-guided sites, all modified or all unmodified at these locations, opening the possibility that modification of these sites by U24 snoRNP is highly processive.
source: Instead, two main populations of ribosomes are observed, all modified or all unmodified at these locations, opening the possibility that modification of these sites by U24 snoRNP is highly processive.
evidence: This is stated as an observation that supports the processive model.

claim: In this view, when the site is accessible all three sites become methylated without dissociation of the U24 snoRNP from the pre-ribosome.
source: In this view, when the site is accessible all three sites become methylated without dissociation of the U24 snoRNP from the pre-ribosome.
evidence: This is stated as part of the processive model.

claim: In Dbp3 mutants and wild-type cells, most U24 is associated with the pre-ribosome.
source: In Dbp3 mutants and wild-type cells, most U24 is associated with the pre-ribosome (Aquino et al., 2021), suggesting that either (1) there are three high-affinity binding sites at which release and rebinding of U24 occurs distributively at a rate that prevents detection of partially modified intermediates, or (2) there is a single binding site at which the target nucleotides are bound and methylated processively after a single U24 snoRNP-binding event.
evidence: This is cited from published literature and used to support alternative interpretations.

claim: The authors developed a hidden Markov model-based approach that allows single-molecule profiling and clustering of RNAs to visualize high-level relationships between features in a population of complete molecules.
source: We developed a hidden Markov model-based approach that allows (1) single-molecule profiling and clustering of RNAs to visualize high-level relationships between features in a population of complete molecules, (2) the ability to test for changes in correlations between any given pair of modifications on the same molecule, and (3) a way to estimate the fraction of modification of each site.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the methodological contribution.

claim: The method allows the ability to test for changes in correlations between any given pair of modifications on the same molecule.
source: We developed a hidden Markov model-based approach that allows (1) single-molecule profiling and clustering of RNAs to visualize high-level relationships between features in a population of complete molecules, (2) the ability to test for changes in correlations between any given pair of modifications on the same molecule, and (3) a way to estimate the fraction of modification of each site.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the methodological contribution.

claim: The method provides a way to estimate the fraction of modification of each site.
source: We developed a hidden Markov model-based approach that allows (1) single-molecule profiling and clustering of RNAs to visualize high-level relationships between features in a population of complete molecules, (2) the ability to test for changes in correlations between any given pair of modifications on the same molecule, and (3) a way to estimate the fraction of modification of each site.
evidence: This is stated as a summary of the methodological contribution.

claim: The authors used wild-type rRNA as their fully modified training example, with the understanding that not all wild-type molecules are fully modified.
source: We used wild-type rRNA as our fully modified training example, with the clear understanding that not all wild-type molecules are fully modified (Taoka et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a methodological choice with acknowledgment of its limitation.

claim: Positions where the signal-to-noise ratio between unmodified and modified nucleotides is small are less accurately predicted compared to other positions.
source: Positions where the signal-to-noise ratio between unmodified and modified nucleotides is small are less accurately predicted compared to other positions.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the method.

claim: Another limitation arises when the training samples do not have enough information to resolve dense clusters of modifications.
source: Another limitation arises when the training samples do not have enough information to resolve dense clusters of modifications.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the method.

claim: Generating more specific modification training data sets that contain all combinations of partially modified closely spaced clusters of nucleotides may be required to produce more accurate and general modification detection algorithms.
source: While there is some evidence that unknown modified kmer distributions can be estimated using known kmer distributions (Ding et al., 2021), generating more specific modification training data sets that contain all combinations of partially modified closely spaced clusters of nucleotides may be required to produce more accurate and general modification detection algorithms.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion for future improvement.

claim: The capture of and profiling of pre-rRNA intermediates, nascent chromatin-associated pre-rRNA, and rRNA turnover products will further resolve and enhance understanding of how the concerted placement and timing of rRNA modifications occurs during the lifetime of the ribosome.
source: While our analysis focuses on mature, full-length rRNA, the capture of and profiling of pre-rRNA intermediates, nascent chromatin-associated pre-rRNA, and rRNA turnover products will certainly further resolve and enhance our understanding of how the concerted placement and timing of rRNA modifications occurs during the lifetime of the ribosome.
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion for future work.

claim: Alterations of rRNA modification have been detected in human diseases and cancer.
source: Recently, alterations of rRNA modification have been detected in human diseases and cancer (Babaian et al., 2020; Barros-Silva et al., 2021; Janin et al., 2020), suggesting that monitoring of concerted changes in rRNA modification might serve as important biomarkers for human disease.
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: Monitoring of concerted changes in rRNA modification might serve as important biomarkers for human disease.

claim: The model training paradigm developed can easily be applied to other nucleic acids of interest.
source: Importantly, the model training paradigm we have developed to profile modifications can easily be applied to other nucleic acids of interest.
evidence: This is stated as a claim about the generalizability of the method.

claim: Recent advancements in nanopore sequencing of full-length human rRNAs and E. coli tRNAs make these heavily modified molecules ripe for single-molecule profiling.
source: Recent advancements in nanopore sequencing of full-length human rRNAs (Jain et al., 2021) and E. coli tRNAs (Thomas et al., 2021) make these heavily modified molecules ripe for single-molecule profiling to understand how RNA modifications regulate translation (Erales et al., 2017; Krogh et al., 2016; Schimmel, 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a suggestion for future applications citing recent work.

claim: It is becoming increasingly clear that modifications of pre-mRNAs and the snRNAs within the splicing machinery are important for regulating alternative splicing and misregulation of modifications are associated with disease.
source: Furthermore, it is becoming increasingly clear that modifications of pre-mRNAs and the snRNAs within the splicing machinery are important for regulating alternative splicing and misregulation of modifications are associated with disease (Bartosovic et al., 2017; Lin et al., 2016; Zheng et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from published literature.

claim: The ability to monitor the modification status at each position across an mRNA molecule, along with its alternative splicing pattern, will become increasingly important for basic biological understanding and discovery.
source: Thus, the ability to monitor the modification status at each position across an mRNA molecule, along with its alternative splicing pattern (Drexler et al., 2020; Tang et al., 2020), will become increasingly important for basic biological understanding and discovery.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction about future importance citing recent work.
